newsitem.title: KAZAKHSTAN: Kazakh May inflation at all time low of 0.4 pct.
newsitem.headline: Kazakh May inflation at all time low of 0.4 pct.

text.p: Kazakhstan's monthly consumer price inflation for May slowed to 0.4 percent, the lowest since the start of market economic reforms in 1992, an official at the National Statistics Agency said on Friday.

"This is the lowest indicator since the start of market reforms," said the agency official who declined to be named. "The next lowest was 0.7 percent in August last year (1996)," she said. Agency indicators published on Friday showed inflation for April this year was 0.8 percent while in May 1996, prices grew by 2.0 percent.
The agency's monthly report provided the following data for Kazakhstan's consumer price inflation.

Due to the National Bank's tight monetary policy, inflation nosedived to 28.7 percent last year from over 2,200 percent in 1992, when the Central Asian state liberalised prices, launching market reforms.
The National Bank's target for this year's inflation is 17 percent, but it has repeatedly said it might fall below this.
